title: HMAC WC_HW_E on INIT failure at Final is correct — CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE would be an auth bypass
description: In crypto2dev_hmac() Final path: if CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_INIT fails and ret==NOT_COMPILED_IN, the code promotes to WC_HW_E rather than CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE. This is correct: the SETKEY callback returned 0 (claiming the key), so wolfSSL's own ipad/opad schedule was skipped. If CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE were returned here, wolfSSL's wc_HmacFinal fallback would compute HMAC with all-zero key and return it as a valid MAC. The port header documents this with 'CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE is NOT safe: HMAC SETKEY returns 0 (claiming the key), so wolfSSL skips its software ipad/opad schedule'. The wc_static_assert2(WC_HW_E \!= CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE) in the port ensures these can never collide. A future contributor might change WC_HW_E to CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE to 'allow fallback' — this would be catastrophically wrong. The assert and the comment both protect this correctly.
